evidence.note: Front-loaded understanding stage: network sizes, reference alignment inspection, degree stats — a distinct sub-goal before building anything.

Scorer built THEN validated by scoring the provided reference alignment first — a done-check tying the metric implementation to the thresholds before an aligner exists; correct sequencing (scorer before optimizer).
Baseline aligner milestone: TaskCreate 'Build C aligner', write sana.c, compile, short test run + verify scoring — a gated checkpoint before optimization.
Yeast deliverable saved/verified and 'locked = ya3' once its S3/NC targets were met, treating the two deliverables as separate milestones with their own thresholds.
After locking yeast, effort is budgeted overwhelmingly toward the harder S3-only DM-HS target (250+ steps of optimization), showing difficulty-weighted allocation across deliverables.
'Save fallback DM-HS and validate' and 'Save z1 fallback' — preserving validated intermediate results as fallback branches while continuing to optimize.

reasoning: The agent exhibits the full level-8 pattern: explicit ordered milestones (understand → scorer validated against reference → baseline aligner verified → optimize to numeric thresholds), each with a concrete done-check and sensibly sequenced (the scorer is validated before the optimizer is built). It exceeds pure level-8 by budgeting effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (yeast locked at step 118 once targets met, then ~250 steps devoted to the harder DM-HS S3 goal) and by keeping validated fallback saves (steps 106, 256, 376) with gating on measured scores before advancing. It stops just short of a fully crisp per-milestone fallback hierarchy, so 9 rather than 10.
